blocked_sentences: If a creature dealt damage this way would die this turn, exile it instead
Any number of target creatures you control phase out

needs.what: A replacement effect, lasting for the rest of the turn and scoped to the set of creatures this spell damaged, that changes where a creature goes when it would die: 'if [these creatures] would die this turn, exile [them] instead'. Two pieces the engine has neither of: (a) a turn-duration mark on an object recording 'this was dealt damage by this source', and (b) an authorable hook at the moment a creature is put into the graveyard from the battlefield that can redirect the destination to exile. Anger of the Gods, Flame Sweep-style exile wraths, Merciless Eviction's cousins and Rest in Peace-adjacent 'exile instead of dying' effects all want the same hook.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `ReplacementModel` (src/automtg/cards/schema.py:202) is a three-value Literal -- `self_enters`, `self_enters_tapped`, `self_enters_with_counters` -- and its own docstring calls itself 'one of the four whitelisted replacement effects'. Every one is about a permanent *entering*; this is the moment one leaves, and there is no `event` spelling for it. The engine does have a death-replacement site, `zones.destroy` (src/automtg/engine/zones.py:320), but it is hard-coded to exactly three mechanisms -- indestructible, a regeneration shield, totem armor -- none of them reachable from a card's own text, and its docstring says so explicitly ('checked here rather than as `replacements` entries because that whitelist is about a permanent entering'). Worse for this card, the lethal-damage state-based action does not route through `destroy` at all: `sba._creature_deaths` (src/automtg/engine/sba.py:264) calls `move_object(..., Zone.GRAVEYARD, cause='lethal_damage')` directly, so the very deaths this card is about would bypass a hook added to `destroy`. Nothing in `ops`, `static_effects` or `trigger_events` substitutes. `damage` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_life.py:57) takes only `amount`/`objects`/`player`/`target` -- there is no exile rider on it. The nearest authorable shape is a delayed trigger on `dies` filtered by `damaged_by`, and it is a *different card*: the creature would really die, its dies-triggers and any 'whenever a creature dies' on the board would all fire, and it would sit in the graveyard long enough to be seen there before being exiled -- which is precisely what a replacement effect exists to prevent. `delay` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_control.py:361) cannot even do that much: a `DelayedTrigger` fires at a named *step*, not on an event, so it has no way to react to a death when the death happens. And an instant has no `abilities` list to hang a lasting triggered ability on anyway -- its effects live in `spell_effects` and are gone when it resolves.

needs.what: An effect op that phases a permanent out on demand -- 'target creature phases out', the one-shot half of phasing, as printed on Teferi's Veil, Vanishing, Reality Acid's cousins and every 'phase out' blink-substitute. It should phase the permanent out immediately (and phase it back in before its controller's next untap step), taking whatever is attached to it along, exactly as the keyword already does.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Phasing shipped as a *keyword read by the untap step* and nothing else. `engine/turn.py` owns the whole mechanism -- `_phase_out` at line 278 and `_phase_in` are module-private, and the only caller is the untap-step walk at line 274, which toggles permanents whose derived keywords contain `phasing`. Grep confirms it: outside `turn.py`, the only mentions of `phased_out` anywhere in `src/` are the two field declarations on `GameObject` (src/automtg/engine/objects.py:218,222). There is no registered op for it -- the complete op registry (every `@register` in `engine/effects/`) has 79 entries and none of them is `phase_out`. The two workarounds both make a different card: `grant_keyword: phasing` gives the creature the *keyword*, which does nothing now and then flickers it out and back on every one of its controller's untap steps forever after -- it neither phases out this turn nor stops next turn; and `exile` plus a `delay` to return it is a real zone change, so the creature loses its counters, its Auras, its damage and its 'continuously on the battlefield' status, triggers every leave- and enter-the-battlefield ability on the table, and comes back as a new object -- the four things docs/rules-coverage.md's phasing row spends its whole argument establishing that phasing does *not* do.

needs.what: A target spec with an unbounded, caster-chosen size -- 'any number of target creatures you control', as on Cryptic Command's cousins, Aetherize-style bounces and every 'any number of target' spell. The count is chosen as the spell is cast and may be zero; today a spec's size is a compile-time constant.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `TargetModel.count` is `int = 1` (src/automtg/cards/schema.py:71) -- a fixed number baked into the card, not a value the caster picks. `engine/targeting.py:150` enumerates `itertools.combinations(options, min(spec.count, len(options)))`, i.e. subsets of *exactly* that size, so there is no representation of a variable-size selection at any layer. `optional: true` adds precisely one extra option, the empty tuple, so `count: N, optional: true` is 'exactly N, or none' -- not 'up to N' and certainly not 'any number'. Picking some large N and calling it 'any number' is an approximation twice over: it caps a printed unbounded choice, and it forbids every size between 1 and N-1. Strictly this need is smaller than the other two -- No More would still be unwritable with it solved, because the phase-out op is what the sentence's verb is -- but it is a separate vocabulary item that blocks the sentence on its own and is worth closing independently.
